prerequisites: No specific prior knowledge of the subject is required, as this is a basic and introductory course.

learning_outcomes.text: Adequate knowledge of the concept of business, its institutional and legal framework. Business organization and management.

Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Students should have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in competence CG01.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to adapt to new situations.
Ability to plan the creation and operation of a company.
Frame the company within the economic reality and economic systems.
Differentiate the various types of companies existing in Spanish legislation.
Distinguish the areas of the company.
Recognize the administrative functions performed in a company.
Know the differences between a balance sheet and an income statement.
Describe various sources of company financing.
Evaluate investment projects.
Calculate and interpret efficiency measures: costs and productivity.
Analyze the various types of productive designs.
Analyze business dimension: break-even point.
Recognize the different existing plant layouts.
Develop a methodology for analyzing how to execute a job.
Calculate the necessary times for performing a job.
Solve and interpret production planning and scheduling techniques.
Recognize the different variables of the marketing-mix.

syllabus_topics: Topic 01. The company and the economic system: Concept of economy, The transformation curve, Fundamental economic problems, Economic systems, Economic agents, Introduction to market functioning.

Topic 02: The company as an economic reality: Concept of company, Company functions, Constituent elements of the company, Classification of companies, Companies according to their legal form, Concept of entrepreneur, The entrepreneur in the reality of the current company. Entrepreneurs, Corporate social responsibility.

Topic 03: The company as a system. Management functions: Concept and properties of systems, Typology of systems, Conceptual elements of the company as a system, Company subsystems, Business environment, Management functions.
Topic 04: The financial function: investment and financing: Fundamental prior concepts, Planned investment, Sources or means of financing in the company, Equity, Debt, Profit and profitability.
Topic 05: Marketing in the company: The commercial subsystem. Definition of marketing, The market: concept, segmentation and strategies, The marketing-mix, Product, Price, Distribution, Promotion.

Topic 06: The production subsystem: Productive activity: concept and classes, Concept and elements of the production subsystem, Types of productive processes, Objectives and decisions in production administration.
Topic 07: Efficiency in the company: Efficiency measures, Productivity, Factors affecting productivity, Concept and classifications of costs.

Topic 08: Dimension of facilities: Concept and criteria for measuring dimension, Dimension and economies of scale, Dimension and cost structure, Dimension, occupancy rate and cost hysteresis, Methodology for determining productive capacity.

Topic 09: Location decisions for facilities: Location decisions for the company and its facilities, Multi-plant location strategies, Procedure and factors for making location decisions, Quantitative location methods.
Topic 10: Physical layout of facilities: Concept, objectives and factors of plant layout, Types of plant layout, Methods of facility layout.
Topic 11: Work design and measurement: Work design, Work methods study, Time study.
Topic 12: Project planning, scheduling, and control: Concept and stages of project management, Concept and types of control, Scope of control, Project planning and control techniques.
teaching_methods: Lectures: In large group sessions, the theoretical foundations of the subject will be explained. In class, the concepts of each topic will be developed, and practical material will be provided to students to apply the acquired knowledge. Appropriate technical means will be used in lectures. The content developed in lectures may be complemented with various bibliographic sources.
Practices, seminars and problems: In practical classes, various types of activities will be proposed: problem solving using techniques explained in the large group, individual work, and group work.

Non-contact learning activities: With the guidance of the subject's professors, students must carry out a series of non-contact activities that complete the competency acquisition process designed for the subject. These activities include: autonomous study (individual or in groups), search for bibliography and resources both individually and in groups for the completion of the different proposed activities.
Tutoring activities: Personal or small group attention to students to advise them on various aspects related to the development of the subject.
Assessment activities: Final theoretical and practical exam.
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on two theoretical exams (50% total) and two practical exams (50% total). Each theoretical exam, covering specific topics, accounts for 25% and includes multiple-choice questions (correct +1, incorrect -0.33) and short answers. Each practical exam also accounts for 25% and consists of exercises where responses must be correct, exact, and reasoned. No resit arrangements or minimum marks are explicitly stated.
